question: What is the primary fluid collected during a lumbar puncture?
explanation: A lumbar puncture specifically targets the subarachnoid space to draw and analyze cerebrospinal fluid. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h1)

question: A physician performs a lumbar puncture to deliver medication directly into which body space?
explanation: Medications administered during this procedure go directly into the subarachnoid or intrathecal space to target the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h1)

question: Between which vertebrae is a lumbar puncture typically performed to avoid spinal cord injury?
explanation: The L3-L4 and L4-L5 interspaces are chosen because they lie safely below the termination of the adult spinal cord. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why does needle insertion low in the lumbar spine prevent damage to the main spinal cord?

options.A: There is no cerebrospinal fluid located in the lower lumbar region.
options.B: Thick muscle layers completely protect the lower spinal nerves.
options.C: The lumbar vertebrae are fused and block deep needle penetration.
options.D: The adult spinal cord ends higher up near the first lumbar vertebra.

explanation: Because the spinal cord terminates around L1, needles placed further down pass safely through the loose nerve roots of the cauda equina instead. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which condition is an absolute safety hazard that can lead to brain herniation during a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Elevated intracranial pressure from a brain tumor
options.B: A history of uncomplicated tension headaches
options.C: Mild essential hypertension controlled with medication
options.D: Chronic lower back pain without neurological signs

explanation: Releasing CSF pressure from the lumbar spine when intracranial pressure is high creates a dangerous pressure gradient that can herniate the brainstem. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check coagulation profile results before a patient undergoes a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To prevent the formation of a spinal epidural hematoma
options.B: To calculate the correct amount of local anesthetic needed
options.C: To ensure the patient will not experience post-puncture headaches
options.D: To check if the patient has an active central nervous infection

explanation: Bleeding disorders put patients at high risk for spinal hematomas, which can compress the spinal cord and cause permanent paralysis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h3)

question: What immediate action should a nurse ask the patient to take just before a lumbar puncture begins?
explanation: An empty bladder minimizes discomfort and prevents accidental incontinence while the patient holds a tight flexed posture. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h4)

question: A patient scheduled for a lumbar puncture expresses extreme fear about paralysis. What is the best initial nursing response?

options.A: Contact the doctor immediately to cancel the scheduled test
options.B: Assure the patient that complications never happen to anyone
options.C: Explain that the needle enters well below the main spinal cord
options.D: Tell the patient that worrying will only make the procedure harder

explanation: Providing accurate, reassuring anatomical facts helps alleviate unfounded fears of paralysis caused by needle contact with the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for placing a patient in a curled fetal position for a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To prevent the patient from moving their legs
options.B: To widen the spaces between adjacent vertebrae
options.C: To decrease blood pressure during needle insertion
options.D: To make it easier to monitor heart rhythm

explanation: Curling the spine flexes the vertebrae apart, providing a wider target window for the clinician to advance the spinal needle. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is a key responsibility of the nurse while assisting a patient during a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Hold the spinal needle steady while the doctor measures pressure
options.B: Label the CSF collection tubes with laboratory barcodes in order
options.C: Administer a general sedative intravenously before the procedure starts
options.D: Maintain the patient in a safe, flexed position and watch their breathing

explanation: Patient movement risks needle displacement or trauma, so the nurse must physically support the position while watching for signs of distress. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is a standard post-procedure instruction often given to patients after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Consume a high sodium diet to replace lost electrolytes
options.B: Lie flat in bed for a prescribed period
options.C: Keep the head elevated at a 45-degree angle
options.D: Walk around the ward immediately to aid circulation

explanation: Lying flat helps reduce the incidence of post-dural puncture headaches by minimizing pressure changes in the spinal column. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why does a nurse regularly check a patient's lower extremities for movement and sensation after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: To evaluate how well the patient tolerated the lateral position
options.B: To ensure the patient has not developed deep vein thrombosis
options.C: To detect early signs of nerve root irritation or hematoma
options.D: To confirm that the local anesthetic has completely worn off

explanation: Monitoring motor and sensory function helps catch rare complications like spinal hematoma or nerve trauma before permanent damage occurs. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: A dull morning headache accompanied by sudden projectile vomiting
options.B: A sharp pain focused entirely behind the eyes and across the jaw
options.C: A headache that worsens when sitting upright and improves when lying flat
options.D: A constant throbbing pain that is unaffected by body position changes

explanation: Post-dural puncture headaches are classic orthostatic headaches caused by low CSF pressure when upright. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary mechanism that causes a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: An allergic reaction to the antiseptic solution used on the skin
options.B: Inflammation of the meninges caused by exposure to room air
options.C: Temporary lack of oxygen reaching the frontal lobe during the test
options.D: Continued leakage of cerebrospinal fluid through the dural puncture site

explanation: Fluid leaking faster than it is produced lowers intracranial pressure, pulling on pain-sensitive cranial structures when the patient sits up. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the normal appearance of healthy cerebrospinal fluid collected during a lumbar puncture?
explanation: Healthy CSF looks clear and colorless, often described as resembling clean water. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h8)

question: Which CSF laboratory finding strongly suggests a bacterial infection of the central nervous system?

options.A: Decreased glucose level and elevated white blood cells with predominant neutrophils
options.B: Decreased protein level combined with normal opening CSF pressure
options.C: Elevated glucose level and zero detectable white blood cells in all tubes
options.D: Clear appearance with normal protein levels and high red blood cell counts

explanation: Bacterial pathogens consume glucose rapidly and provoke a large neutrophil response, resulting in low glucose and high neutrophil counts in the CSF. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h8)
